key_insight: In melanoma image classification, the choice of loss function materially affects both discrimination and calibration, with focal loss offering the best overall balance in this study.
clinical_relevance: For AI-assisted melanoma triage, better-calibrated models may support more reliable risk estimates and downstream decision-making, especially in imbalanced datasets.
method: Compared focal loss, logit-adjusted softmax cross-entropy, and weighted softmax cross-entropy.
Trained deep neural networks on the SIIM-ISIC melanoma classification dataset.
Evaluated both predictive performance and uncertainty calibration metrics.
evidence_signal: Across the reported evaluation metrics, focal loss achieved a strong AUC while also showing favorable expected calibration error (ECE).
watch_item: Results come from an imbalanced melanoma dataset, so performance and calibration may not transfer directly without revalidation on other clinical datasets or deployment settings.
paper_title: On Impact of Loss Function on the Performance of Neural Networks in Melanoma Diagnosis
